criteria.criterion: docs/design/scope-guard.md states the value-versus-cost test: value side names failure class, goal or product need, and how often it bites, each with a source; cost side gives expected dollars and wall time labeled measured or estimate; a decision rule says when work is queued, merged, deferred or dropped.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff. Section 3.1 has a table of value inputs (failure class, goal or need, frequency, already done) with a 'Source it must cite' column. Section 3.2 gives expected dollars and wall time, each labeled measured or estimate. Section 3.3 has a decision table with Drop, Merge, Defer, Queue and Queue (doubt) rows. Its anchors ($1.67 and $2.50) match job-planning.md lines 235-236.

criteria.criterion: The design grounds itself in the record with these figures, each labeled as supplied by the request (records/ not visible to the producer) unless a repository source is cited: trailer job, three rejected attempts and about 11 dollars before the split; about 80 minutes lost to the prompt-budget trap; 49 open requests, many done or superseded; test-suite speedup, three rejected attempts (jobs 20261025-190606-eebk, 20261025-202447-xgk9, 20261025-214509-y179, about 9 dollars and 4 hours), each a real gain (test check about 12 to 7.4-7.8 minutes) but rejected for missing a fixed time target set without a measurement showing it reachable, then landed by narrowed request 20261025-230352-ph40; cut A took four tries (timing race, wait on wrong check, duplicate push-triggered runs).
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff. Section 4 lists every figure, each marked **(request)**. Where it cites the repository I checked the source: D126 (decisions.md lines 3138-3160) names eebk, xgk9 and y179, with about 651 s before and 392 s after, and 444-466 s against 720 s. D125 (line 3107) is the push-trigger change.

criteria.criterion: Thrash signals have numeric thresholds with stated basis or an 'estimate, to be tuned' label, covering repeated retries, growing plans, cost against forecast p90, and a line of work rejected twice for the same unmet criterion; the document shows which signals would have fired on the trailer job, the speedup and the prompt-budget trap.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff. Section 5 lists signals T1-T5 with thresholds, each with a basis or labeled an estimate. T4 is 'same criterion rejected twice'. The replay in section 5.1 covers the trailer job, the speedup, the prompt-budget trap and cut A. It shows T4 firing after the second speedup rejection (xgk9), before y179, and T5 firing at 60 minutes on the trap. The per-attempt dollar figures follow from the stated even-split estimate.

criteria.evidence: Read in the diff. Section 6 has lists headed 'Code decides', 'A model scores and writes', a 'Why' paragraph, and 'A model verdict may not', which covers pauses, flags, the table, the quota, Sri-only items and governance files.

criteria.criterion: Powers are listed: what it can stop or merge on its own, what is advisory, what goes to Sri and through which channel; learnings work (BRIEF.md addendum 2026-10-25) is not blocked, via a protected quota, default-to-proceed on doubt, and an appeal path.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff. Section 8 lists own authority (defer, merge exact duplicates, pause and never kill, flag), advisory actions, and items for Sri. findings.summary: The decision table has a gap: work with value 0 and expected cost of $1 or less (and not learnings work) matches no row.
findings.evidence: Drop needs value 0 and cost over $1. Queue needs value 1, 2 or 3. Defer needs value 1, or cost over p90. A cheap value-0 request is left undecided. It is also unclear whether the 'Drop' row, which comes first in rule order, takes precedence over 'Queue (doubt)' for learnings work with an empty value record.
